notes: How alike two cases must be before recorded experience is allowed to inform a new one. These are operational judgements, not engineering constants. Symptom overlap outweighs entity identity deliberately: what is happening is more diagnostic than where it is happening. Weighting them the other way reproduces anchoring bias, where a familiar component presenting an unfamiliar symptom attracts the familiar diagnosis.

transfer.notes: Experience observed elsewhere can never count as fully as experience observed here. A structural sibling is strong evidence and still an analogy.
